messages:
Alex: quick sync — CI started failing on the integration suite after we bumped some deps. Tests that exercise the Python SDK async streaming are throwing weird AttributeError / typing failures. anyone seen this? :eyes:

Maria: can you paste the traceback and your pyproject / pip freeze? usually sounds like httpx/httpcore mismatch or an import path change.

Alex: traceback snippet:
```
AttributeError: 'AsyncClient' object has no attribute 'stream'
  File "tests/integration/test_stream.py", line 42, in test_streaming
    async for event in client.stream(...):
AttributeError: 'AsyncClient' object has no attribute 'stream'
```
pyproject deps (excerpt):
```toml
[tool.poetry.dependencies]
python = "^3.10"
redwood-sdk = "^0.8.0"
httpx = "^0.25.0"
```
pip freeze shows httpx==0.25.1, httpcore==0.18.0, typing-extensions==4.6.0

Jaz: that stack smells like httpx version changed API. httpx used to expose `AsyncClient.stream` but newer versions changed streaming helpers (or the SDK wrappers rely on a particular behavior). Also if the SDK vendor expects httpcore pinned you can get runtime errors.

Nina: also check pip vs poetry lock mismatch. If CI does `pip install -r requirements.txt` but your local uses `poetry install`, lockfile export differences cause mismatched transitive httpcore.

Alex: hmm CI installs from constraints file we generate from poetry lock. command is `poetry export -f requirements.txt --without-hashes --output constraints.txt` then `pip install -c constraints.txt -r requirements.txt` — shouldn't that keep them aligned?

Maria: yes but if you bumped httpx in pyproject *without* regenerating the lock, the exported constraints can still carry old transitive pins. try `poetry lock --no-update` or `poetry lock` then export again. Also make sure your CI's poetry version matches (older poetry has different resolver).

Jaz: quick workaround for CI: pin httpx/httpcore explicitly in pyproject, e.g. `httpx = "0.24.*"` and `httpcore = "0.16.*"` (pick the pair that the SDK was tested with). Then regenerate lock and re-export.

Nina: type hints part: mypy complaining? For httpx there's no official stub package, types are in the package but some internal classes changed names; you may need to add `mypy.ini` ignores for library stubs until we standardize on a single httpx. Example `mypy.ini` tweak:
```ini
[mypy]
ignore_missing_imports = True
```
short-term you can narrow ignores to `# type: ignore[import]` near the import.

Alex: we also saw `AttributeError` not just mypy — so runtime first. i'm going to try the pin + lock regen.

(15s later) Alex: quick test locally — downgraded httpx to 0.24.1 and httpcore to 0.16.3, ran the failing test, streaming works again.

Maria: nice. can you open a tiny PR that pins those in pyproject (with a comment referencing this thread) and run full CI? i'll review.

Jaz: also flag to eng-ml/runtime that SDK needs a compatibility test matrix for httpx/httpcore so future bumps don't break consumers. maybe add a CI job that runs SDK tests against multiple httpx/httpcore pairs.

Alex: will do PR now. also updated our contributor guideline note to remind people to `poetry lock && poetry export` before raising a dep bump PR.

ci-bot: build started for branch alex/pin-httpx (job 9342) :building_construction:

Nina: once CI passes, can someone add a one-line changelog entry under `changelog/unreleased` so releases team knows why pinning happened?

Alex: yep — added changelog in the PR. thanks all :thumbsup:

Maria: fyi for anyone else running into this: if you're on older pip, dependency resolver bugs can cause installs to ignore constraints; upgrade pip to latest in CI `python -m pip install --upgrade pip` — saved us previously.

Alex: closing this thread when CI green. thanks for the quick help!
